column1: # Shekyl cryptographic domain-separation registry (SA-3b) — SINGLE SOURCE.
# Every production domain-separation byte-string in the Rust workspace, grouped
# by the ONE keyed/hashing mechanism that consumes it. This file is consumed by
# BOTH:
#   - scripts/ci/domain_registry_gate.sh  (row-presence + per-mechanism count-pins)
#   - rust/shekyl-crypto-pq/tests/domain_registry.rs  (intra-mechanism distinctness)
# so the census cannot silently drift from the code for *registered* rows: a
# value change, rename, or move breaks row-presence (+ const binding); a new
# always-domain call site (cSHAKE / FROST) breaks the count-pin; an accidental
# equality breaks distinctness. New unregistered domains in general-purpose
# mechanisms (HKDF / Blake2b / keccak / SHA3-256) are a review duty, not a
# gate guarantee — see the gate header and CBOM §3. Prefix-grep is NOT used —
# domain spellings share no common prefix (shekyl/, shekyl-, "Shekyl ",
# "Monero ", bulletproof), which is exactly the SA §3.1 defect class; the
# mechanism entry point is the only complete anchor.
# THROUGH-LINE INVARIANT (SA, ratified): a live domain string's BYTES are
# consensus / derivation state, not a naming convention. Style inconsistency
# across these rows is intended and permanent. "Aligning" a live string's
# spelling is the KAT-remint error at consensus stakes — see
# docs/design/SIGNATURE_ALIGNMENT.md §5. This registry pins the bytes precisely
# so a future "cleanup" cannot touch them without failing the gate.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated):
#   mech    1..6 mechanism id (see below); "x" = excluded-with-reason
#   literal exact bytes WITHOUT the b"" wrapper (the gate greps for b"<literal>")
#   file    repo-root-relative path where the literal is DEFINED (the b"..." site)
#   const   defining constant name, or a short site descriptor in parens
#   status  shekyl-live | frozen-inherited | excluded | test-only
#   key     distinctness identity within the mechanism; empty => defaults to <literal>
#   notes   free text
# Per-mechanism row counts are NOT annotated here — they are derivable state,
# pinned once (and checked against the parsed rows) in
# rust/shekyl-crypto-pq/tests/domain_registry.rs. A second hand-counted copy
# would drift and then lie.
# MECHANISMS:
#   1  cSHAKE256 customization        (shekyl_crypto_hash::cshake256_*, CShake256Core::new)
#   2  HKDF salt + info               (Hkdf::new(Some(salt)..), .expand(info,..)); distinctness key = salt|info
#   3  FROST transcript label         (RecommendedTranscript::new, .domain_separate, Curve::CONTEXT/ID)
#   4  Blake2b DST                    (first Blake2b512::update as a domain; sal_dst-padded tags)
#   5  keccak / schnorr challenge DST (schnorr sign/verify domain, keccak256(...) hash-to-point/scalar prefix)
#   6  SHA3-256 direct-prefix         (micro-bucket: a domain prefix fed straight to Sha3_256, outside 1..5)
# SUB-LABELS ARE OUT OF SCOPE (documented, not rowed): FROST transcript field
# labels appended via append_message (b"O_tilde", b"r_o", ...), the schnorr
# nonce/challenge sub-labels (b"nonce", b"R", ...), and HKDF composed-salt
# sub-components (b"mainnet"/b"testnet"/b"stagenet"/b"fakechain", b"bip39"/b"raw32").
# These never stand alone as a top-level context; they are structural fields
# inside one of the mechanisms above.
# EXCLUDED (named, NOT silently dropped) — real byte-strings that are NOT
# cryptographic domain separation for our purposes: RandomX Argon salt
# (RANDOMX_ARGON_SALT, RandomX upstream), Tor SAFECOOKIE HMAC keys, the .onion
# checksum prefix, file/wire magics (b"SWSP", b"SHEKYLWT/WS", b"SSP1"
# superscalar-program wire magic, portable_storage header). Rowed at the
# bottom with mech=x so the exclusion is auditable. (The C++ epee macros
# PORTABLE_STORAGE_SIGNATUREA/B in contrib/epee are the same 8-byte signature
# as the first 8 bytes of `shekyl-portable-storage::HEADER`; the registry is
# a Rust-workspace census, so only the Rust defining site is rowed.)

column1: # ── TEST-ONLY — domains minted by test/bench code, segregated from production ─
# Registered so the SEGREGATION is machine-checked: a test-only domain spelled
# equal to a live production domain in the same mechanism would let a
# test-minted artifact (signature, KAT vector) verify against the production
# context — cross-context replay of test artifacts. The distinctness test
# (test_domains_are_segregated_from_production) asserts every row here is
# disjoint from the production identities of its mechanism. Test-vs-test
# collisions are NOT policed (two tests may legitimately share a dummy domain).
# Completeness has the same review-duty scope as mech 2/4/5/6: register new
# test domains as they are minted; the census below is as of 2026-08-11.
# (b"" — cshake256_32's empty-customization compatibility test in
# shekyl-crypto-hash — is not rowed: the parser requires a non-empty literal,
# and production domains are non-empty, so it cannot collide.)
# ── EXCLUDED — named, not domain separation for our purposes ────────────────
